name: fleet_sonnet_macro_sector_rotation
strategy: Catalyst-driven sector rotation book going into the 2026-09-16 FOMC: trim the un-confirmed biotech-M&A long, add ballast via low-volatility, and lean harder into the two legs the tape has actually validated -- the regional-bank/financials longs and the semis short -- while nudging the discretionary short up on continuing earnings weakness, cash raised slightly ahead of the event.
reassessment_note: Research this session (Fed funds futures, and cross-checked against a sibling desk book's independent pull of the same data) puts roughly 90% odds on the FOMC landing in the 3.75-4.00% band on 2026-09-16, i.e. the meeting itself is largely priced and unlikely to be the shock that moves this book -- the bigger risk into the print is sector-specific positioning, so I am de-risking the weakest, least-confirmed leg and reinforcing the two that the tape is actually confirming rather than doing a wholesale rewrite. XBI is trimmed from 14% to 8%: price is still sliding (down another ~2% today per Yahoo, on top of the -3.82% already booked on this leg) and this week's news flow shows no confirmed M&A catalyst -- the original thesis leg of this book -- only ETF-comparison pieces and a note that retail biotech sentiment is 'never been lower.' That sentiment extreme is a real contrarian signal, which is why I am not closing the position outright, but conviction is lower than when it was sized at 14%, so the position is cut roughly in half. SMH short is increased from 5% to 10%: the leg is already the book's best performer (+4.58% on the current fill) and this week's coverage adds concrete confirming evidence rather than just momentum exhaustion -- 'bearish shape' technical pattern calls plus South Korea's Kospi (a chip-heavy index) reportedly plunging into earnings, both landing on top of SMH's already-extreme +57.9% YTD run that leaves it priced for perfection. XLY short is raised from 6% to 9%, continuing the standing thesis (confirming discretionary earnings weakness) with no new information this session to change course, just conviction sizing. XLV, XLF and KRE (16/13/14%) are held essentially flat -- KRE and XLF are both modestly green on the week (KRE +0.55%, roughly flat entry-to-mark on XLF) and a Fed outcome that holds rates rather than cutting is generally a neutral-to-supportive backdrop for bank net interest margins, so there is no information here that argues for cutting bank exposure into the event. SPLV (low-volatility) is raised from 4% to 6% as explicit ballast for event-day volatility around the statement and press conference. Gross exposure is raised slightly from 72% to 76% (cash trimmed from 28% to 24%) to fund the SMH/XLY conviction adds, with the XBI trim freeing most of the room; net effect is a modestly larger, more polarized book (bigger short book, smaller unconfirmed long) rather than a larger net-long one. This book has zero overlap with the Round 2 macro book (GLD/FXI only), so the novelty rule is satisfied by construction regardless of this rebalance.

positions.thesis: Cut from 14% to 8%. Original thesis was biotech M&A catalyst; this week's news flow shows no confirmed deal activity, only sector-comparison commentary, and the ETF kept sliding (down ~2% today, -3.82% on the standing leg). Kept rather than closed because retail biotech sentiment is reported at an extreme low, which is historically a contrarian setup, but conviction no longer justifies the prior 14% size without a confirmed catalyst.

Held flat. Broad healthcare defensiveness is a reasonable ballast leg into an FOMC print that is largely priced (~90% odds of landing at 3.75-4.00%); the leg is barely underwater (-0.29%) and nothing in this week's research argues for cutting a low-beta core holding.

Held flat. Financials broadly track the bank-long thesis; a Fed that holds rates rather than cutting is a neutral-to-supportive setup for lending margins, and the leg is only marginally negative (-0.66%), so there is no fresh signal to reduce here.

Held flat. This is the book's confirmed winner among the bank longs: KRE is up 0.55% today and the leg is essentially flat-to-positive versus entry. Regional banks are the most rate-path-sensitive names in the book, so this is the position most worth carrying unchanged through the actual FOMC statement rather than pre-empting it.

Raised from 4% to 6% as explicit low-volatility ballast for FOMC-day price action -- a small increase, funded by the XBI trim, to dampen the book's swings on the one day this week with a genuine scheduled catalyst.

Raised from 6% to 9%, continuing the standing discretionary-earnings-weakness thesis (already profitable at +1.75% on the current fill) with higher conviction sizing; no new contradicting data surfaced this session, and a Fed that holds rather than cuts keeps consumer financing costs elevated, which is consistent with, not against, this leg.

Raised from 5% to 10%. Already the book's best leg (+4.58%), and this week adds concrete confirming evidence beyond the entry thesis: technical commentary flagging a bearish chart pattern in semiconductors, plus reports of South Korea's Kospi (chip-heavy) plunging into earnings season -- both sitting on top of SMH's extreme +57.9% YTD run that leaves the group priced for perfection and most exposed if the FOMC's holds-rather-than-cuts outcome pressures high-multiple growth names.
